author: mafas
quote: In Brazil, GTA VI costs almost a third of the minimum monthly wage. I won't lie, I've played approximately 6 hours so far, but considering two criteria I value highly, storytelling and gameplay mechanics, which I'll discuss further below, the game has been extremely disappointing. It has gorgeous graphics and impressive attention to detail, but that was already expected. We're talking about a production with an estimated investment of over $1 billion, using advanced technology and years of development. Visual polish was the bare minimum. What really bothers me is that certain mechanics and design decisions give me the impression that the game was built with a future online mode in mind. Some things simply feel strange and out of place. It doesn't feel like GTA. As for the story... the brilliant Bonnie and Clyde concept feels like it has been completely thrown away. Lucia is **** annoying, while Jason is extremely passive. It's as if they took the most extreme aspects of each personality and exaggerated them to the point of absurdity. And even though they can sometimes work well together and actually make for an entertaining duo, individually, I'd say they're insufferable roughly 85% of the time. GTA has always had strong personalities, YES! But there's a difference between memorable characters and characters who are simply exhausting to deal with. In Vice City and GTA IV, we had protagonists with very distinct identities, deep stories and, at times, genuinely melancholic narratives. Meanwhile, GTA V and San Andreas leaned much more heavily into comedy, exaggeration and ridiculous humor, but still managed to make their characters work. GTA VI seems to be trying to combine these approaches, but at least during my first few hours, it fails at fundamental aspects that a franchise like GTA, especially under Rockstar's direction, simply should not get wrong. And to make matters worse, we also have the return of an extremely important character from a previous installment, in a decision that, in my opinion, completely undermines the narrative development of his past and the weight of his own story's conclusion. It's simply frustrating to see a franchise that has always placed so much importance on character development make decisions that seem to disregard precisely what made those stories so memorable. My score is much more a statement of disappointment over wasted potential than a straightforward technical assessment. The graphics, the details and the Easter eggs were already expected. And enough with the hypocrisy, because if companies like Activision, EA, Ubisoft or even Bethesda released games today, got the things they're traditionally good at right, but failed at the one thing that actually matters, fun and entertainment, you'd be dragging their scores down too. ENOUGH WITH THIS MEDIOCRE GENERATION OF GAMES! WE WANT INNOVATION, BETTER GAMEPLAY, NEW AND UNIQUE MECHANICS, FUN AND, ABOVE ALL, WE DON'T WANT PRODUCTS, WE WANT GAMES!
